title: Morning in Camp
sceneText:
There is a cold light coming through the canvas. You wake in the camp far stiffer in the bones than you would have from a bed.

The fire has gone out; there is ash left, and a few attendants still asleep. Birds somewhere off. Movement over where the horses are.

Henk is already up, standing at the edge of the trees with something hot, his back to the camp.

What you said last night, nobody mentions this morning.

choices.text: Stay, and ride out with today’s hunt

effects.logEntry: You stayed in camp and rode today’s line with the field.

choices.text: Take your leave of Henk and ride back to the estate

effects.logEntry: You took your leave of Henk and rode back to Maplegate.

choices.resultText:
You go to take your leave of Henk.

He is telling two men which line they are taking today, and stops when he sees you coming.

“Off already?”

You say there are things waiting at the estate.

“Fair enough,” he says. “You stayed last night. That is handsome of you.”

He means it. He claps you on the shoulder and turns back to his line.

There is frost on the road home. The horse goes slower than it came.

Most of the morning is gone by the time you reach the estate. The people in the fields went out long ago. Martha is in the kitchen, and she nods when she sees you back, and asks nothing about the hunt.

You still have the afternoon.
